# A PSD diagonal Jensen stress need not be a positive sum of Jensen variances

This is an exact algebraic obstruction on a lattice-convex finite base. It
satisfies a positive null-curvature condition. It does not assert that the
stress is realized by a low-depth active-cap certificate.

## 1. Base, active equalities, and stress

Take P={-1,0,1}^2 and let L be the space satisfying all anchored Jensen
equalities on P. Then

    L={v_(x,y)=a+b x+c y}.

Indeed row and column midpoint equalities first give
v=a+b x+c y+d xy. The diagonal midpoint equality at the center forces d=0.
Conversely every affine function satisfies every anchored equality.

Define the diagonal weights W by

    W_(1,0)=W_(-1,0)=1/2,
    W_(0,1)=W_(0,-1)=2,
    W_(0,0)=-5,
    W_(1,1)=W_(-1,-1)=1/2,
    W_(1,-1)=W_(-1,1)=-1/2.

Their zeroth and first moments vanish. Their second-moment matrix is

    sum_z W_z z z^T = [[1,2],[2,4]].

Consequently

    sum_z W_z v_z^2=(b+2c)^2 >=0                         (1)

for every v in L. The strictly positive vector r_z=1 belongs to its
nullspace. If a convention requires W_z<=1, replace every W by W/2;
all conclusions persist.

## 2. No positive Jensen-variance decomposition exists even as a form

A nontrivial anchored representation z=sum_w p_w w gives on L the variance
form

    V_(z,p)(v)=sum_w p_w v_w^2-v_z^2
       =(b,c) C_(z,p) (b,c)^T,
    C_(z,p)=sum_w p_w (w-z)(w-z)^T >=0.

Suppose (1) were a positive combination of such variance forms. The sum of
their covariance matrices would be the nonzero rank-one matrix
(1,2)(1,2)^T. Testing against a vector perpendicular to (1,2) shows that
every positively weighted covariance has range contained in span(1,2).
Because each covariance is a sum of nonnegative rank-one matrices, every
source w with p_w>0 must then lie on the line z+R(1,2).

But a line parallel to the primitive integer vector (1,2) contains at most
two points of the 3x3 grid. A nontrivial anchored convex representation
along that line would require at least two distinct source points and the
distinct anchor between them, hence at least three grid points. This is
impossible. All such variance generators would therefore be zero,
contradicting the nonzero target matrix.

Thus even after allowing arbitrary coefficient-vector identities that
vanish on L, the PSD quadratic form does not have a positive Jensen-
variance decomposition. The obstruction is stronger than failure to
represent its particular diagonal coefficient vector.

## A variant with positive stress on every extreme base vertex

The same second-moment matrix and quadratic form arise from

    W_(1,1)=W_(-1,-1)=5/4,
    W_(1,-1)=W_(-1,1)=1/4,
    W_(1,0)=W_(-1,0)=-1,
    W_(0,1)=W_(0,-1)=1/2,
    W_(0,0)=-2.

Every extreme base vertex has strictly positive weight; all negative weights
are at nonvertices that can be genuine Jensen anchors. The unavailable
rank-one direction still precludes every positive variance decomposition.
Multiplication by 4/5 also enforces W_z<=1 without changing the conclusion.

## 3. The positive nullspace can carry nonhomothetic smooth arcs

The nullspace of (1) inside L consists of

    v_z=a+t(2x-y),

and has dimension two. For example, choose R>9 epsilon>0 and define

    h_(x,y)(theta)=R+epsilon(2x-y)cos(2theta).

These are support functions of smooth strictly convex planar bodies,
because their curvature radii are

    r_(x,y)(theta)=R-3 epsilon(2x-y)cos(2theta)>0.

Every support and curvature vector lies in L, and every curvature vector
lies in the nullspace of the SAME fixed PSD stress. The fibers with
different values of 2x-y are not homothetic translates: the constant
Fourier coefficient is fixed R while the second harmonic varies.

All support equalities are actual compatible equalities, since h is affine
in the base coordinate. The resulting family is the set of fibers of the
bounded convex body defined over [-1,1]^2 by the corresponding support
halfplanes. Thus the algebraic nullspace behavior is compatible with
actual convex fiber geometry, although no active-cap realization of W is
claimed.

This example rules out forcing a one-dimensional homothetic nullspace or a
positive Jensen-variance decomposition from PSD and positive null curvature
alone. It is consistent with broader affine-component structure; here the
whole family is already affine in the base coordinates.
